parsedOutput.title: One-Pan Chicken Thighs with Rice and Carrots
parsedOutput.description: A simple, one-pan dinner that cooks everything together. Chicken thighs stay juicy while rice and carrots soften in the pan juices.
parsedOutput.story: This recipe uses common pantry staples to create a hearty meal with minimal cleanup. The chicken fat renders into the rice, adding rich flavor without extra oil.

instructions.body: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Pat chicken thighs dry and season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown, about 5 minutes. Flip and cook for 2 more minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
In the same pan, add diced onions and carrots. Sauté for 5 minutes until onions soften. Stir in garlic and thyme, cooking for 1 minute.
Add the rinsed rice and chicken broth to the pan. Stir to combine. Place the seared chicken thighs back on top, skin-side up.
Cover the skillet tightly with a lid. Transfer to the oven and bake for 25-30 minutes, or until rice is tender and chicken is cooked through.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving. Fluff the rice with a fork and serve chicken with the vegetables and rice.

instructions.body: Cook rice according to package directions. Set aside.
In a small bowl, whisk together peanut butter, water, lemon juice, garlic powder, and salt until smooth.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add broccoli and a splash of water. Cover and steam for 5 minutes until tender-crisp.
Add chickpeas to the skillet. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until heated through.
Divide cooked rice among four bowls. Top with broccoli and chickpeas.
Drizzle the peanut sauce evenly over the bowls and serve immediately.
